draft.question_en: Can entities use AI systems for national security, military, and defense purposes even if these systems are intended for civilian or law enforcement use?
draft.question_fr: Peut-on utiliser des systèmes d'IA pour des fins de sécurité nationale, militaire et de défense, même si ces systèmes sont destinés à des fins civiles ou de police ?
draft.ground_truth: Entities can use AI systems for national security, military, and defense purposes even if these systems are intended for civilian or law enforcement use.
draft.key_facts: AI system, national security, military, defence, civilian, law enforcement
draft.evidence: An AI system placed on the market for civilian or law enforcement purposes which is used with or without modification for military, defence or national security purposes should not fall within the scope of this Regulation, regardless of the type of entity carrying out those activities.

draft.question_en: What group should be established to support the implementation and monitoring of the AI Act, and what are the key responsibilities of its members?
draft.question_fr: Quel groupe devrait être établi pour soutenir la mise en œuvre et le contrôle du règlement AI, et quelles sont les principales responsabilités de ses membres ?
draft.ground_truth: Un groupe scientifique composé d’experts indépendants devrait être établi. Les experts devraient être choisis en fonction de leur expertise dans le domaine de l’IA, s’acquitter de leurs tâches avec impartialité et objectivité, et veiller à la confidentialité des informations et des données obtenues dans l’exercice de leurs tâches et activités.
key_facts: expertise dans le domaine de l’IA
s’acquitter de leurs tâches avec impartialité et objectivité
veiller à la confidentialité des informations et des données
draft.evidence: Les experts indépendants constituant le groupe scientifique devraient être choisis en fonction de leur expertise à la pointe des connaissances scientifiques ou techniques dans le domaine de l’IA. Ils devraient s’acquitter de leurs tâches avec impartialité et objectivité et veiller à la confidentialité des informations et des données obtenues dans l’exercice de leurs tâches et activités.

draft.question_en: Can entities involved in national security, defence, and military activities use AI systems for these purposes even if they are placed on the market for civilian or law enforcement use?
draft.question_fr: Peut-on que des entités impliquées dans les activités de sécurité nationale, de défense et de military utilisent des systèmes d'IA pour ces activités même si ceux-ci sont mis sur le marché pour des usages civils ou de police ?
draft.ground_truth: Entities carrying out national security, defence and military activities can use AI systems for these purposes even if the systems are placed on the market for civilian or law enforcement purposes.
draft.evidence: An AI system placed on the market for civilian or law enforcement purposes which is used with or without modification for military, defence or national security purposes should not fall within the scope of this Regulation, regardless of the type of entity carrying out those activities.

draft.question_en: What should independent experts in the scientific or technical field of AI be chosen for in the context of the AI Act?
draft.question_fr: Quels experts indépendants dans le domaine scientifique ou technique de l'IA devraient-ils être choisis dans le contexte du règlement AI ?
draft.ground_truth: Les experts indépendants constituant le groupe scientifique devraient être choisis en fonction de leur expertise à la pointe des connaissances scientifiques ou techniques dans le domaine de l’IA.
key_facts: choisis en fonction de leur expertise
concernant les modèles d’IA à usage général
draft.evidence: Les experts indépendants constituant le groupe scientifique devraient être choisis en fonction de leur expertise à la pointe des connaissances scientifiques ou techniques dans le domaine de l’IA.

section: PART THREE CAPITAL REQUIREMENTS > TITLE II CAPITAL REQUIREMENTS FOR CREDIT RISK > CHAPTER 2 Standardised Approach > Section 2 Risk weights

draft.question_en: What percentage of the value of the pledged properties must be composed of residential mortgages combined with any prior liens when senior units are used as collateral?
draft.question_fr: Quelle proportion de la valeur des biens hypothéqués doit être composée de prêts hypothécaires résidentiels combinés avec n'importe quel gage préalable lorsque des unités senior sont utilisées comme garantie?
draft.ground_truth: At any time while they are included in the cover pool, the assets underlying such units shall, at any time while they are included in the cover pool be at least 90 % composed of residential mortgages that are combined with any prior liens up to the lesser of the principal amounts due under the units, the principal amounts of the liens, and 80 % of the value of the pledged properties.
draft.evidence: at any time while they are included in the cover pool be at least 90 % composed of residential mortgages that are combined with any prior liens up to the lesser of the principal amounts due under the units, the principal amounts of the liens, and 80 % of the value of the pledged properties

section: 4. Guidelines on outsourcing > Title II – Assessment of outsourcing arrangements > 4 Critical or important functions

draft.question_en: What must institutions consider when assessing the criticality or importance of functions in outsourcing arrangements?
draft.question_fr: Quels facteurs doivent les institutions prendre en compte lors de l'évaluation de la criticité ou de l'importance des fonctions dans les arrangements de cession?
draft.ground_truth: Institutions and payment institutions should consider a function as critical or important in the following situations: where a defect or failure in its performance would materially impair their continuing compliance with the conditions of their authorisation or its other obligations under various directives and regulations; their financial performance; or the soundness or continuity of their banking and payment services and activities; when operational tasks of internal control functions are outsourced, unless the assessment establishes that a failure to provide the outsourced function or the inappropriate provision of the outsourced function would not have an adverse impact on the effectiveness of the internal control function; when they intend to outsource functions of banking activities or payment services to an extent that would require authorisation by a competent authority; and when assessing whether an outsourcing arrangement relates to a function that is critical or important, institutions and payment institutions should take into account, together with the outcome of the risk assessment outlined in Section 12.2, at least the following factors.
key_facts: soundness or continuity of their banking and payment services and activities
draft.evidence: Institutions and payment institutions should always consider a function as critical or important in the following situations: where a defect or failure in its performance would materially impair: their continuing compliance with the conditions of their authorisation or its other obligations under Directive 2013/36/EU, Regulation (EU) No 575/2013, Directive 2014/65/EU, Directive (EU) 2015/2366 and Directive 2009/110/EC and their regulatory obligations; their financial performance; or the soundness or continuity of their banking and payment services and activities;

section: ANNEX VII Conformity based on an assessment of the quality management system and an assessment of the technical documentation

draft.question_en: What must a provider include in their application to a notified body under the AI Act?
draft.question_fr: Quelles informations doit le fournisseur inclure dans sa demande à un organisme notifié selon l'AI Act ?
draft.ground_truth: The application shall include: the name and address of the provider; a written declaration that the same application has not been lodged with any other notified body; the technical documentation referred to in Annex IV.
key_facts: name and address of the provider
technical documentation referred to in Annex IV
draft.evidence: 4.2. The application shall include: (a) the name and address of the provider; (b) a written declaration that the same application has not been lodged with any other notified body; (c) the technical documentation referred to in Annex IV.

section: ANNEX VIII Information to be submitted upon the registration of high-risk AI systems in accordance with Article 49

draft.question_en: What information must be provided by the deployer of a high-risk AI system under Article 49(3)?
draft.question_fr: Quelles informations doivent être fournies par le déployeur d'un système d'IA à haut risque en vertu de l’article 49(3) ?
draft.ground_truth: The deployer must provide the name, address and contact details of the deployer, the name, address and contact details of the person submitting information on behalf of the deployer, the URL of the entry of the AI system in the EU database by its provider, a summary of the findings of the fundamental rights impact assessment, and a summary of the data protection impact assessment, where applicable.
key_facts: name, address and contact details of the deployer
name, address and contact details of the person submitting information on behalf of the deployer
URL of the entry of the AI system in the EU database by its provider
summary of the findings of the fundamental rights impact assessment conducted in accordance with Article 27 of the AI Act
draft.evidence: The following information shall be provided and thereafter kept up to date with regard to high-risk AI systems to be registered in accordance with Article 49(3): 1. The name, address and contact details of the deployer; 2. The name, address and contact details of the person submitting information on behalf of the deployer; 3. The URL of the entry of the AI system in the EU database by its provider; 4. A summary of the findings of the fundamental rights impact assessment conducted in accordance with Article 27; 5. A summary of the data protection impact assessment carried out in accordance with Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 or Article 27 of Directive (EU) 2016/680 as specified in Article 26(8) of this Regulation, where applicable.

section: ANNEXE IV Documentation technique visée à l'article 11, paragraphe 1

draft.question_en: What must be included in the technical documentation for an AI system according to the AI Act?
draft.question_fr: Quels éléments doivent figurer dans la documentation technique d'un système d'IA selon l'AI Act ?
draft.ground_truth: Le règlement sur l'IA exige une description détaillée des modifications prédéterminées du système d'IA et de ses performances, les procédures de validation et d'essai, les mesures de cybersécurité, des informations détaillées sur la surveillance, le fonctionnement et le contrôle du système d'IA, une description de l'adéquation des indicateurs de performance, une description détaillée du système de gestion des risques, et une description des modifications pertinentes apportées par le fournisseur au système tout au long de son cycle de vie.
key_facts: surveillance, fonctionnement et contrôle du système d'IA détaillés
draft.evidence: [AI ACT · ANNEXE IV Documentation technique visée à l'article 11, paragraphe 1] f) le cas échéant, une description détaillée des modifications prédéterminées du système d'IA et de ses performances, ainsi que toutes les informations pertinentes relatives aux solutions techniques adoptées pour garantir que continue d'être assurée la conformité du système d'IA aux les exigences pertinentes énoncées au chapitre III, section 2; g) les procédures de validation et d'essai utilisées, y compris les informations sur les données de validation et d'essai utilisées et leurs principales caractéristiques; h) les mesures de cybersécurité qui ont été prises;

section: CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

draft.question_en: What does the term 'AI system' mean according to the AI Act?
draft.question_fr: Quel est le sens du terme 'système d’intelligence artificielle' selon le règlement sur l'IA?
draft.ground_truth: An AI system means a machine-based system that is designed to operate with varying levels of autonomy and that may exhibit adaptiveness after deployment, and that, for explicit or implicit objectives, infers, from the input it receives, how to generate outputs such as predictions, content, recommendations, or decisions that can influence physical or virtual environments.
key_facts: operates with varying levels of autonomy
infers, from the input it receives, how to generate outputs such as predictions, content, recommendations, or decisions that can influence physical or virtual environments
draft.evidence: "AI system’ means a machine-based system that is designed to operate with varying levels of autonomy and that may exhibit adaptiveness after deployment, and that, for explicit or implicit objectives, infers, from the input it receives, how to generate outputs such as predictions, content, recommendations, or decisions that can influence physical or virtual environments;

section: CHAPTER X CODES OF CONDUCT AND GUIDELINES

draft.question_en: What specific requirements can codes of conduct cover for AI systems under the AI Act?
draft.question_fr: Quelles exigences spécifiques peuvent couvrir les codes de conduite pour les systèmes d'IA selon le règlement sur l'IA?
draft.ground_truth: Codes of conduct may cover one or more AI systems taking into account the similarity of the intended purpose of the relevant systems.
key_facts: taking into account the similarity of the intended purpose
draft.evidence: Codes of conduct may cover one or more AI systems taking into account the similarity of the intended purpose of the relevant systems.

section: CHAPITRE IV OBLIGATIONS DE TRANSPARENCE POUR LES FOURNISSEURS ET LES DÉPLOYEURS DE CERTAINS SYSTÈMES D’IA

draft.question_en: What must providers of AI systems that generate synthesized content do to mark their outputs?
draft.question_fr: Quels doivent être les fournisseurs de systèmes d’IA qui génèrent des contenus de synthèse de type audio, image, vidéo ou texte pour marquer leurs sorties?
draft.ground_truth: Les fournisseurs de systèmes d’IA, y compris de systèmes d’IA à usage général, qui génèrent des contenus de synthèse de type audio, image, vidéo ou texte, veillent à ce que les sorties des systèmes d’IA soient marquées dans un format lisible par machine et identifiables comme ayant été générées ou manipulées par une IA.
key_facts: marquées dans un format lisible par machine
identifiables comme ayant été générées ou manipulées par une IA
draft.evidence: Les fournisseurs de systèmes d’IA, y compris de systèmes d’IA à usage général, qui génèrent des contenus de synthèse de type audio, image, vidéo ou texte, veillent à ce que les sorties des systèmes d’IA soient marquées dans un format lisible par machine et identifiables comme ayant été générées ou manipulées par une IA.

section: PART TWO OWN FUNDS > TITLE I ELEMENTS OF OWN FUNDS > CHAPTER 2 Common Equity Tier 1 capital > Section 3 Deductions from common equity tier 1 items, exemptions and alternatives

draft.question_en: Under CRR, which conditions must be met for an institution not to deduct the holdings of own funds instruments of a financial sector entity in which it has a significant investment?
draft.question_fr: Selon le CRR, quelles conditions doivent être remplies pour que l'institution ne doive pas déduire les titres propres détenus dans une entité du secteur financier dans laquelle elle a un investissement significatif?
draft.ground_truth: The institution must be an insurance undertaking, re-insurance undertaking or insurance holding company, included in the same supplementary supervision, have received prior permission from the competent authorities, and the level of integrated management, risk management and internal control is adequate, and the holdings belong to specific entities.
key_facts: same supplementary supervision under Directive 2002/87/EC as the parent institution, parent financial holding company or parent mixed financial holding company or institution that has the holding, prior permission of the competent authorities, level of integrated management, risk management and internal control is adequate, holdings belong to one of the following: the parent credit institution, the parent financial holding company, the parent mixed financial holding company, the institution, a subsidiary of one of the entities referred to in points (i) to (iv) that is included in the scope of consolidation pursuant to Chapter 2 of Title II of Part One
draft.evidence: For the purposes of calculating own funds on an individual basis, a sub-consolidated basis and a consolidated basis, where the competent authorities require or permit institutions to apply method 1, 2 or 3 of Annex I to Directive 2002/87/EC, the competent authorities may permit institutions not to deduct the holdings of own funds instruments of a financial sector entity in which the parent institution, parent financial holding company or parent mixed financial holding company or institution has a significant investment, provided that the conditions laid down in points (a) to (e) of this paragraph are met.

section: PART THREE CAPITAL REQUIREMENTS > TITLE II CAPITAL REQUIREMENTS FOR CREDIT RISK > CHAPTER 4 Credit risk mitigation > Section 3 Requirements

draft.question_en: What must institutions do to ensure the enforceability of collateral arrangements under applicable law?
draft.question_fr: Quelles mesures doivent les institutions prendre pour assurer l'efficacité juridique des arrangements de garantie selon la législation applicable?
draft.ground_truth: Institutions shall fulfil any contractual and statutory requirements in respect of, and take all steps necessary to ensure, the enforceability of the collateral arrangements under the law applicable to their interest in the collateral. They shall re-conduct such review as necessary to ensure continuing enforceability.
key_facts: fulfil any contractual and statutory requirements
take all steps necessary to ensure
draft.evidence: Institutions shall fulfil any contractual and statutory requirements in respect of, and take all steps necessary to ensure, the enforceability of the collateral arrangements under the law applicable to their interest in the collateral. They shall re-conduct such review as necessary to ensure continuing enforceability.

section: PART THREE CAPITAL REQUIREMENTS > TITLE II CAPITAL REQUIREMENTS FOR CREDIT RISK > CHAPTER 6 Counterparty credit risk > Section 7 Contractual netting

draft.question_en: What condition must a contractual netting agreement not include to ensure full payment in the event of default?
draft.question_fr: Quelle condition doit l'accord de nettoyage contractuel ne pas inclure pour garantir le paiement intégral en cas de défaut?
draft.ground_truth: The contract shall not contain any clause which, in the event of default of a counterparty, permits a non-defaulting counterparty to make limited payments only, or no payments at all, to the estate of the defaulting party, even if the defaulting party is a net creditor (i.e. walk away clause).
draft.evidence: The contract shall not contain any clause which, in the event of default of a counterparty, permits a non-defaulting counterparty to make limited payments only, or no payments at all, to the estate of the defaulting party, even if the defaulting party is a net creditor (i.e. walk away clause).

section: PART FOUR LARGE EXPOSURES

draft.question_en: What is the additional capital requirement if the excess has not persisted for more than 10 days?
draft.question_fr: Quelle est la provision complémentaire de fonds propres si l'exces n'a pas persisté pendant plus de 10 jours ?
draft.ground_truth: The additional capital requirement shall be 200 % of the requirements referred to in paragraph 1, on these components.
draft.evidence: Where the excess has not persisted for more than 10 days, the additional capital requirement shall be 200 % of the requirements referred to in paragraph 1, on these components.

section: PART TEN TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS, REPORTS, REVIEWS AND AMENDMENTS > TITLE I TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS > CHAPTER 2 Grandfathering of capital instruments > Section 2 Instruments not constituting state aid

draft.question_en: Under CRR, when can Tier 2 items with an incentive to redeem qualify as Tier 2 items?
draft.question_fr: Selon le CRR, sous quels conditions les titres de niveau 2 avec un incitatif de rachat peuvent-ils être considérés comme des titres de niveau 2 ?
draft.ground_truth: Tier 2 items with an incentive to redeem can qualify as Tier 2 items if the institution did not exercise the call on the date of the effective maturity of the items and the conditions set out in Article 63 are not met from that date.
key_facts: institution did not exercise the call
date of the effective maturity of the items
conditions set out in Article 63 are not met
draft.evidence: The items shall qualify as Tier 2 items in accordance with Article 484(5) where: (a) the institution was able to exercise a call with an incentive to redeem only prior to or on 31 December 2011; (b) the institution did not exercise the call on the date of the effective maturity of the items; (c) the conditions laid down in Article 63 are not met from the date of the effective maturity of the items.

draft.question_en: Which entities are exempt from the scope of DORA according to the passage?
draft.question_fr: Quelles entités sont exemptées du champ d’application du DORA selon le passage ?
draft.ground_truth: Certaines entités financières bénéficient d’exemptions ou sont soumises à un cadre réglementaire très léger en vertu du droit sectoriel applicable de l’Union. Ces entités financières comprennent les gestionnaires de fonds d’investissement alternatifs visés à l’article 3, paragraphe 2, de la directive 2011/61/UE du Parlement européen et du Conseil (16), les entreprises d’assurance et de réassurance visées à l’article 4 de la directive 2009/138/CE du Parlement européen et du Conseil (17) et les institutions de retraite professionnelle gérant des régimes de retraite qui, ensemble, n’ont pas plus de quinze affiliés au total.
draft.evidence: Certaines entités financières bénéficient d’exemptions ou sont soumises à un cadre réglementaire très léger en vertu du droit sectoriel applicable de l’Union. Ces entités financières comprennent les gestionnaires de fonds d’investissement alternatifs visés à l’article 3, paragraphe 2, de la directive 2011/61/UE du Parlement européen et du Conseil (16), les entreprises d’assurance et de réassurance visées à l’article 4 de la directive 2009/138/CE du Parlement européen et du Conseil (17) et les institutions de retraite professionnelle gérant des régimes de retraite qui, ensemble, n’ont pas plus de quinze affiliés au total.

draft.question_en: What rights should contracts for critical or important IT service provision include for financial entities or their designated third parties?
draft.question_fr: Quels droits devraient inclure les contrats de fourniture de services TIC critiques ou importants pour les entités financières ou leurs tiers désignés?
draft.ground_truth: Les contrats de fourniture de services TIC qui soutiennent des fonctions critiques ou importantes devraient également contenir des dispositions permettant l’exercice des droits d’accès, d’inspection et d’audit par l’entité financière ou par un tiers désigné, et le droit de prendre des copies.
draft.evidence: Les contrats de fourniture de services TIC qui soutiennent des fonctions critiques ou importantes devraient également contenir des dispositions permettant l’exercice des droits d’accès, d’inspection et d’audit par l’entité financière ou par un tiers désigné, et le droit de prendre des copies en tant qu’outils essentiels pour permettre aux entités financières d’assurer un suivi permanent des performances du prestataire tiers de services TIC, parallèlement à la coopération totale de ce prestataire de services lors des inspections.

section: CHAPITRE II Gestion du risque lié aux TIC > Section II

draft.question_en: What must AESs and ENISA collaborate on to ensure the security of networks and data integrity under DORA?
draft.question_fr: Quels projets communs doivent les AES et l'ENISA élaborer pour garantir la sécurité des réseaux et l'intégrité des données dans le cadre de DORA ?
draft.ground_truth: Les AES élaborent des projets communs de normes techniques de réglementation afin de garantir la sécurité des réseaux, de favoriser la mise en place de garanties adéquates contre les intrusions et les utilisations abusives des données, de préserver la disponibilité, l’authenticité, l’intégrité et la confidentialité des données.
draft.evidence: de préciser davantage les éléments à inclure dans les politiques, procédures, protocoles et outils de sécurité des TIC visés à l’article 9, paragraphe 2, en vue de garantir la sécurité des réseaux, de favoriser la mise en place de garanties adéquates contre les intrusions et les utilisations abusives des données, de préserver la disponibilité, l’authenticité, l’intégrité et la confidentialité des données.

section: CHAPITRE IV Tests de résilience opérationnelle numérique

draft.question_en: What conditions must be met when financial entities use internal testers for penetration tests based on threat?
draft.question_fr: Quelles conditions doivent être remplies lorsque les entités financières utilisent des testeurs internes pour des tests de pénétration fondés sur la menace ?
draft.ground_truth: Les entités financières doivent s'assurer que le recours à ces testeurs internes a été approuvé par l'autorité compétente, que l'entité dispose des ressources suffisantes et que les conflits d'intérêts sont évités, et que le fournisseur de renseignements sur les menaces est externe à l'entité financière.
key_facts: recours à ces testeurs internes a été approuvé
l'entité financière dispose des ressources suffisantes
le fournisseur de renseignements sur les menaces est externe à l'entité financière
draft.evidence: a) le recours à ces testeurs internes a été approuvé par l'autorité compétente concernée ou par l'autorité publique unique désignée conformément à l’article 26, paragraphes 9 et 10; b) l'autorité compétente concernée a vérifié que l’entité financière dispose des ressources suffisantes et a veillé à éviter les conflits d’intérêts pendant les phases de conception et d’exécution du test; et c) le fournisseur de renseignements sur les menaces est externe à l’entité financière.

section: CHAPITRE VII Autorités compétentes

draft.question_en: Who is subject to the duty of confidentiality under DORA Article 55?
draft.question_fr: Qui est soumis à l’obligation de secret professionnel selon l’article 55 de DORA ?
draft.ground_truth: Toutes les personnes qui travaillent, ou ont travaillé, pour les autorités compétentes en vertu du présent règlement, ou pour toute autorité, entreprise de marché ou personne physique ou morale à laquelle ces autorités compétentes ont délégué leurs pouvoirs, y compris les auditeurs et les experts qu’elles ont mandatés.
draft.evidence: L’obligation de secret professionnel s’applique à toutes les personnes qui travaillent, ou ont travaillé, pour les autorités compétentes en vertu du présent règlement, ou pour toute autorité, entreprise de marché ou personne physique ou morale à laquelle ces autorités compétentes ont délégué leurs pouvoirs, y compris les auditeurs et les experts qu’elles ont mandatés.

draft.question_en: What are the key governance impacts of introducing ML in internal credit scoring models?
draft.question_fr: Quels sont les impacts de gouvernance principaux de l'introduction de l'IA dans les modèles internes d'octroi de crédit?
draft.ground_truth: Les impacts de gouvernance principaux de l'introduction de l'IA sont une technicité accrue du processus de validation initiale, la mise en place d'outils de monitoring pour le contrôle interne, et l'intégration de méthodes explicatives.
draft.evidence: Les deux scénarios ont montré l’impact de l’introduction de ML en termes de gouvernance : technicité accrue du processus de validation initiale, mise en place d’outils de monitoring pour le contrôle interne, et intégration de méthodes explicatives.

section: Annexes > 8.1. Atelier « LCB-FT » > 8.1.9. Atelier complémentaire

draft.question_en: What additional condition must be met for an alert to be generated by the ML tool?
draft.question_fr: Quelle condition supplémentaire doit être remplie pour que l'alerte soit générée par l'outil de ML?
draft.ground_truth: Une alerte déclenchée par l’outil de ML est une alerte ayant obtenu un score élevé et qui est passée sous les seuils de détection du moteur de règles métier dans les trois mois précédents.
draft.evidence: Un filtre a été mis en place afin que, lorsqu’une transaction obtient un score élevé par le modèle de ML, une alerte ne soit générée que si aucune alerte n’a été levée par le moteur de règles métier sur ce même client dans les trois mois précédents.

section: Annexes > 11. Recension des méthodes explicatives en IA

draft.question_en: What are the three categories of explainability methods according to the ACPR IA 2020 annexes?
draft.question_fr: Quelles sont les trois catégories des méthodes d’explication selon les annexes de l’ACPR IA 2020 ?
draft.ground_truth: Les méthodes d’explication se répartissent alors classiquement en trois catégories selon la phase de la conception et de l’utilisation du modèle sous-jacent : 1. les méthodes explicatives pré-modélisation visent à comprendre et décrire les données utilisées dans la production des modèles ; 2. les méthodes explicatives conjointes à la modélisation contribuent à la conception de modèles intrinsèquement plus explicables ; 3. enfin, les méthodes explicatives post-modélisation tentent de produire des explications satisfaisantes à partir de modèles préalablement conçus et entraînés.
draft.evidence: Les méthodes d’explication se répartissent alors classiquement en trois catégories selon la phase de la conception et de l’utilisation du modèle sous-jacent : 1. les méthodes explicatives pré-modélisation visent à comprendre et décrire les données utilisées dans la production des modèles ; 2. les méthodes explicatives conjointes à la modélisation contribuent à la conception de modèles intrinsèquement plus explicables ; 3. enfin, les méthodes explicatives post-modélisation tentent de produire des explications satisfaisantes à partir de modèles préalablement conçus et entraînés.

section: 4. Guidelines on outsourcing > Title III – Governance framework > 6 Sound governance arrangements and outsourcing

draft.question_en: What should institutions and payment institutions ensure when outsourcing critical or important functions?
draft.question_fr: Quels sont les garanties que devraient assurer les établissements et les institutions de paiement lors de la cession de fonctions critiques ou importantes?
draft.ground_truth: Institutions and payment institutions should ensure that they can take and implement decisions related to their business activities and critical or important functions, including with regard to those that have been outsourced.
draft.evidence: Institutions and payment institutions should maintain at all times sufficient substance and not become ‘empty shells’ or ‘letter-box entities’. To this end, they should: a. meet all the conditions of their authorisation43 at all times, including the management body effectively carrying out its responsibilities as set out in paragraph 36 of these guidelines; b. retain a clear and transparent organisational framework and structure that enables them to ensure compliance with legal and regulatory requirements; c. where operational tasks of internal control functions are outsourced (e.g. in the case of intragroup outsourcing or outsourcing within institutional protection schemes), exercise appropriate oversight and be able to manage the risks that are generated by the outsourcing of critical or important functions; and d. have sufficient resources and capacities to ensure compliance with points (a) to (c).

section: 4. Guidelines on outsourcing > Title III – Governance framework > 15 Exit strategies

draft.question_en: What should institutions and payment institutions ensure when developing exit strategies for outsourcing critical or important functions?
draft.question_fr: Quels sont les aspects que les institutions et les établissements de paiement doivent assurer lors du développement de stratégies de sortie pour l'externalisation de fonctions critiques ou importantes?
draft.ground_truth: Institutions and payment institutions should ensure that they are able to exit outsourcing arrangements without undue disruption to their business activities, without limiting their compliance with regulatory requirements and without any detriment to the continuity and quality of its provision of services to clients.
draft.evidence: Institutions and payment institutions should ensure that they are able to exit outsourcing arrangements without undue disruption to their business activities, without limiting their compliance with regulatory requirements and without any detriment to the continuity and quality of its provision of services to clients.

section: Guidelines on ICT and security risk management > 3.3. ICT and security risk management framework > 3.3.2. Identification of functions, processes and assets

draft.question_en: What should financial institutions map according to EBA GL 2019 04?
draft.question_fr: Quels éléments devraient les institutions financières identifier selon l'AI Act 2019 04?
draft.ground_truth: Financial institutions should map their business functions, roles, supporting processes, and information assets such as ICT systems, staff, contractors, third parties, and dependencies on other internal and external systems and processes.
draft.evidence: Financial institutions should identify, establish and maintain updated mapping of their business functions, roles and supporting processes to identify the importance of each and their interdependencies related to ICT and security risks. In addition, financial institutions should identify, establish and maintain updated mapping of the information assets supporting their business functions and supporting processes, such as ICT systems, staff, contractors, third parties and dependencies on other internal and external systems and processes, to be able to, at least, manage the information assets that support their critical business functions and processes.

section: Guidelines on ICT and security risk management > 3.7. Business continuity management > 3.7.2. Business continuity planning

draft.question_en: What should financial institutions consider in their business continuity plans to ensure the continuity of ICT systems and services, and the institution’s information security?
draft.question_fr: Quelles scénarios les établissements de crédit doivent-ils prendre en compte dans leurs plans de continuité d'activité pour assurer la continuité des systèmes et services ICT et la sécurité de l'information de l'établissement?
draft.ground_truth: Financial institutions should consider a range of different scenarios, including extreme but plausible ones to which they might be exposed, and assess the potential impact that such scenarios might have. Based on these scenarios, a financial institution should describe how the continuity of ICT systems and services, as well as the financial institution’s information security, are ensured.
key_facts: describe how the continuity of ICT systems and services, as well as the financial institution’s information security, are ensured
draft.evidence: A financial institution should consider a range of different scenarios in its BCP, including extreme but plausible ones to which it might be exposed, and it should assess the potential impact that such scenarios might have. Based on these scenarios, a financial institution should describe how the continuity of ICT systems and services, as well as the financial institution’s information security, are ensured.

section: 4. Internal governance for credit granting and monitoring > 4.3 Credit risk policies and procedures

draft.question_en: What should credit risk policies and procedures include according to the passage?
draft.question_fr: Quels éléments devraient inclure les politiques et procédures de gestion des risques de crédit selon le passage ?
draft.ground_truth: Credit risk policies and procedures should include specific lending policies and procedures, with sufficient granularity to capture the specific business lines of the institution, for different sectors, in line with their varying complexities and sizes, and risks of different market segments related to the credit facility. They should also specify policies and procedures and rules for the approval of credit granting and decision-making, credit-granting criteria, requirements for the handling of information and data needed for the creditworthiness assessment, requirements for the creditworthiness assessment, including a sensitivity analysis, requirements for exposure aggregation and credit risk limits and the management of credit risk concentrations, and requirements and procedures regarding the acceptance and use of collateral and credit risk mitigation measures.
key_facts: requirements for the handling of information and data
requirements for the creditworthiness assessment including a sensitivity analysis
draft.evidence: Credit risk policies and procedures should include specific lending policies and procedures, with sufficient granularity to capture the specific business lines of the institution, for different sectors, in line with their varying complexities and sizes, and risks of different market segments related to the credit facility. They should also specify policies and procedures and rules for the approval of credit granting and decision-making, credit-granting criteria, requirements for the handling of information and data needed for the creditworthiness assessment, requirements for the creditworthiness assessment, including a sensitivity analysis, requirements for exposure aggregation and credit risk limits and the management of credit risk concentrations, and requirements and procedures regarding the acceptance and use of collateral and credit risk mitigation measures.

draft.question_fr: Quels éléments doivent les institutions évaluer lorsque l'accord de prêt comporte des garanties de tiers ?
draft.ground_truth: Institutions should assess the level of protection provided by the guarantee and, if relevant, conduct a creditworthiness assessment of the guarantor, applying the relevant provisions of these guidelines, depending on whether the guarantor is a natural person or an enterprise.

section: 8. Monitoring framework > 8.2 Monitoring of credit exposures and borrowers

draft.question_en: What should institutions do if a leveraged transaction is not syndicated within 90 days of the commitment date?
draft.question_fr: Quelles actions devraient les institutions prendre si une transaction à effet de levier n'est pas syndiquée dans les 90 jours suivant la date de la garantie?
draft.ground_truth: Institutions should identify transactions subject to failed syndications — that is, transaction that were not syndicated within 90 days following the commitment date. Institutions should establish a dedicated framework to deal with these ‘hung transactions’ in terms of holding strategy, booking and accounting practices, regulatory classification and subsequent capital requirements calculation.

section: 4. Guidelines > 5.1 Setting up committees

draft.question_en: Which institutions are required to establish risk, nomination, and remuneration committees according to the EBA guidelines?
draft.question_fr: Quelles institutions sont tenues d'établir des comités de risque, de nomination et de rémunération selon les lignes directrices de l'EBA ?
draft.ground_truth: All institutions that are themselves significant, considering the individual, sub-consolidated and consolidated levels, must establish risk, nomination and remuneration committees.
draft.evidence: 40. In accordance with Article 109(1) of Directive 2013/36/EU in conjunction with Articles 76(3), 88(2), and 95(1) of Directive 2013/36/EU, all institutions that are themselves significant, considering the individual, sub-consolidated and consolidated levels, must establish risk, nomination and remuneration committees to advise the management body in its supervisory function and to prepare the decisions to be taken by this body.

section: 4. Guidelines > 12.2 Documentation of loans to members of the management body and their related parties and additional information

draft.question_en: What additional information must be provided to the competent authority for loans to management body members or their related parties exceeding EUR 200,000?
draft.question_fr: Quelle information supplémentaire doit être fournie au pouvoir compétent pour les prêts accordés aux membres du conseil de direction ou à leurs parties liées excédant 200 000 euros?
draft.ground_truth: For a loan to a member of the management body or their related parties above an amount of EUR 200,000, institutions should be able to provide to the competent authority upon request the following additional information: a. the percentage of the loan and the percentage of the sum of all outstanding amounts of loans towards the same debtor compared to: i. the sum of its Tier 1 capital and Tier 2 capital and ii. common equity Tier-1 capital of the institution; b. whether the loan is part of a large exposure; and c. the relative weight of the aggregated sum of all outstanding amounts of loans towards the same debtor, calculated as a percentage by dividing the total outstanding amount by the total amount of all outstanding loans to members of the management body and their related parties.
key_facts: the percentage of the sum of all outstanding amounts of loans towards the same debtor
the sum of its Tier 1 capital and Tier 2 capital and common equity Tier-1 capital of the institution (in that order)
draft.evidence: For a loan to a member of the management body or their related parties above an amount of EUR 200 000, institutions should be able to provide to the competent authority upon request the following additional information: a. the percentage of the loan and the percentage of the sum of all outstanding amounts of loans towards the same debtor compared to: i. the sum of its Tier 1 capital and Tier 2 capital and ii. common equity Tier-1 capital of the institution; b. whether the loan is part of a large exposure; and c. the relative weight of the aggregated sum of all outstanding amounts of loans towards the same debtor, calculated as a percentage by dividing the total outstanding amount by the total amount of all outstanding loans to members of the management body and their related parties.

section: 4. Guidelines > 18 New products and significant changes43

draft.question_en: What should an institution's new product approval policy (NPAP) cover according to the guidelines?
draft.question_fr: Quels aspects devrait couvrir la politique d'approbation des nouveaux produits (NPAP) selon les directives?
draft.ground_truth: An institution's NPAP should cover the development of new markets, products, and services, significant changes to existing ones, and material changes to related processes and systems. It should also ensure that approved products and changes are consistent with the risk strategy and risk appetite of the institution and the corresponding limits of the institution.
key_facts: development of new markets, products and services
material changes to related processes and systems
draft.evidence: An institution should have in place a well-documented new product approval policy (NPAP), approved by the management body, that addresses the development of new markets, products and services, and significant changes to existing ones, as well as exceptional transactions. The policy should in addition encompass material changes to related processes (e.g. new outsourcing arrangements) and systems (e.g. IT change processes).

section: Annex I– Principle-based recommendations Recommendations regarding the regulatory compliant use of ML techniques in the context of the IRB framework

draft.question_en: What should institutions avoid when using ML models to ensure model explainability and simplicity?
draft.question_fr: Quels sont les choses que les institutions doivent éviter lors de l'utilisation de modèles ML pour assurer la simplicité et l'explicabilité du modèle?
draft.ground_truth: Institutions should avoid including an excessive number of explanatory drivers or drivers with no significant predictive information, using unstructured data if more conventional data is available that provides similar predictive capacities, and overly complex modelling choices if simpler approaches yielding similar results are available.
key_facts: including an excessive number of explanatory drivers
draft.evidence: Institutions are recommended to avoid: a. including an excessive number of explanatory drivers or drivers with no significant predictive information; b. using unstructured data if more conventional data is available that provides similar predictive capacities; and c. overly complex modelling choices if simpler approaches yielding similar results are available.
